sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
transliteration: karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stvakarmaṇi
meaning: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself the cause of the results, nor be attached to inaction.
explanation: Anxiety is born from anticipating outcomes we cannot control. When you dedicate your attention purely to the present effort rather than obsessing over success or failure, mental turmoil dissolves.
practical_guidance: Identify one current worry about future results. Consciously shift your focus strictly to the immediate next physical action you can take.

transliteration: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ | āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata
meaning: The contact of the senses with their objects gives rise to fleeting feelings of heat and cold, happiness and pain. These experiences are impermanent, appearing and disappearing; learn to endure them patiently.
explanation: Intense emotions like anxiety and distress feel permanent in the moment, but they are transient waves of experience. Practicing emotional patience (titiksha) allows storms to pass without consuming you.
practical_guidance: Observe physical sensations of tension without fighting them. Remind yourself: 'This emotional wave has a beginning, a peak, and an inevitable end.'

sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते। सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
transliteration: dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate | saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate
meaning: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment to them. From attachment arises craving, and from unfulfilled craving, anger is born.
explanation: Anger rarely occurs in isolation; it is almost always the grief of a blocked expectation or desire. Tracing anger back to what you were expecting gives you clarity and control.
practical_guidance: Ask yourself: 'What expectation did I hold that was just violated?' Disarm the anger by accepting the reality of the moment before reacting.

sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः। स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति॥
transliteration: krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ | smṛti-bhraṁśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati
meaning: From anger arises delusion, from delusion comes loss of memory and grounding. When memory is lost, intellect and reason are destroyed; and when reason is lost, a person falls.
explanation: Anger acts as an emotional blindfold that hijacks cognitive clarity. Acknowledging that anger destroys wisdom prompts us to pause before speaking or deciding in heat.
practical_guidance: Implement a mandatory 10-breath pause or physically step away when anger flares before writing an email or engaging in argument.

sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे। गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः॥
transliteration: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṁ prajñā-vādāṁś ca bhāṣase | gatāsūn agatāsūṁś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
meaning: You grieve for that which is not worthy of grief, yet you speak words of apparent wisdom. The truly wise mourn neither for the living nor for the departed.
explanation: Deep sadness often stems from clutching onto things, roles, or relationships whose essential nature is change. Realizing that the inner self is beyond destruction relieves sorrow.
practical_guidance: Acknowledge sorrow without identifying as a helpless victim. Ask: 'What enduring core within me remains untouched despite this loss?'

sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
transliteration: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṁ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
meaning: The soul is never born, nor does it ever perish. It does not cease to be, nor does it come into existence anew. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting, and primeval; it is not slain when the body dies.
explanation: In times of existential loneliness, despair, or grief, remember that your essential consciousness is invulnerable to external wounds and failures.
practical_guidance: Place your hand over your chest, feel your steady breathing, and recognize that you are the observer of sorrow, not the sorrow itself.

sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते। क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप॥
transliteration: klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate | kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
meaning: Do not yield to unmanliness and paralysis, O son of Pritha; it is unworthy of you. Shake off this trivial weakness of heart and stand up, O scorcher of foes!
explanation: Fear seeks to paralyze us by magnifying our vulnerabilities. Krishna commands Arjuna not to deny fear, but to rise above the paralysis by remembering his innate strength.
practical_guidance: Stand up straight, take three deep diaphragmatic breaths, and take the single most courageous action you have been avoiding today.

sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
transliteration: uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet | ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
meaning: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, and not degrade oneself. The mind is indeed the friend of the conditioned soul, and the mind is also its enemy.
explanation: Your own mind has the power either to torment you with self-doubt and fear, or to guide you as a compassionate friend. Reclaiming control of inner dialogue is your sacred duty.
practical_guidance: Notice your internal dialogue right now. Is your self-talk acting as a supportive ally or a destructive adversary? Refocus it gently toward kindness.

sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्। ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्॥
transliteration: yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram | tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṁ nayet
meaning: From whatever direction the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, one should gently rein it in and bring it back under the control of the Self.
explanation: A wandering, anxious mind is natural. Meditation and peace do not mean having zero distracting thoughts; they mean patient, non-judgmental redirection back to the center.
practical_guidance: Whenever you catch your thoughts spiraling into catastrophizing, don't get angry with yourself. Softly bring your attention back to your breath.

sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः। न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन॥
transliteration: nāty-aśnatas tu yogo 'sti na caikāntam anaśnataḥ | na cāti-svapna-śīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna
meaning: Yoga is not possible for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats too little; nor for one who sleeps too much or one who stays awake excessively.
explanation: Well-being thrives on the golden mean of moderation. Extreme lifestyle swings exacerbate anxiety and deplete resilience.
practical_guidance: Review your baseline physical inputs today: have you had adequate water, nourishing food, and sufficient sleep? Steady the body to steady the mind.

sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः। स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति॥
transliteration: yo 'ntaḥ-sukho 'ntar-ārāmas tathāntar-jyotir eva yaḥ | sa yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṁ brahma-bhūto 'dhigacchati
meaning: One whose happiness is within, who delights within, and whose light shines from within—such a yogi attains liberation in the supreme, being attuned to all existence.
explanation: External conditions will forever oscillate between favorable and difficult. Anchoring your joy in inner contentment liberates you from reliance on external validation.
practical_guidance: List three simple blessings or qualities within yourself right now that do not depend on external praise or outcomes.

sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम्। तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्॥
transliteration: yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam | tat sukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam
meaning: That happiness which in the beginning feels like poison, but in the end tastes like nectar, is called Sattvic (pure), born of the serene awakening of self-realization.
explanation: True and enduring peace often demands self-discipline and confronting uncomfortable truths upfront. Fleeting pleasure tastes sweet first and turns bitter; lasting joy starts with quiet effort.
practical_guidance: Celebrate the quiet satisfaction of having completed a difficult duty or practice today, rather than chasing quick temporary distractions.

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय। सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते॥
transliteration: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya | siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga ucyate
meaning: Perform your duties established in yoga, renouncing attachment, remaining balanced in both success and failure. Such equanimity of mind is called Yoga.
explanation: Equanimity (samatvam) is the supreme definition of spiritual practice. When you treat wins and losses with the same calm poise, life loses its power to destabilize you.
practical_guidance: Pause and breathe into a space of emotional neutrality. Remind yourself: 'Success does not elevate my true worth, and failure does not diminish it.'

sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः। हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः॥
transliteration: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ
meaning: One by whom no one is agitated, and who is not agitated by the world, who is freed from excessive excitement, impatience, fear, and anxiety—that person is very dear to Me.
explanation: Emotional mastery is a double pledge: neither perturbing those around you nor allowing the turbulence of the world to shatter your inner equilibrium.
practical_guidance: Practice remaining an unagitated presence for someone close to you today. Let your steadiness act as an anchor.
